findings.reason: Verified in impl.go: SetDefault runs at line 87 before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so a device rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached stays cached and the next requests within 29 minutes return nil, letting it through.

wire.go:374-375 still lists anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore, which now needs an unprovided int64 and is no longer consumed, so wire generation would fail; the claim that the plain Go build regenerates wire_gen.go is wrong since wire.go is wireinject-tagged, but the generation breakage is real.

Verified that a missing X-Grafana-Device-Id returns nil and grants anonymous access without a limit check, but the body is a design question about intent rather than a defect the PR clearly gets wrong.
Count and upsert are separate sessions with no transaction, so concurrent new devices can exceed the limit; the race is real but the limit is soft and the impact is modest.

Verified the goroutine was removed so tagging now runs synchronously with a COUNT on each cache miss, and a client disconnect cancels the write after the cache key was already set, so the device is skipped for 29 minutes; the same SetDefault-before-write root cause as finding 0.
The test gap is real: no re-submission of a known device at the limit and no TagDevice/Authenticate test, which would have caught the cache bypass verified in finding 0.
Confirmed hide_version is documented in conf/defaults.ini and sample.ini while device_limit is not, but this is a documentation omission only.
The typing and unused-field observations are correct (int64 has no omitempty, and nothing under public/ reads it), but this is a cleanup-level style point with no defect.
